input: Research dual enrollment options for my high schooler

gold.taskTitle: Research Dual Enrollment Options for Your High Schooler
gold.taskDescription: Find and evaluate dual enrollment programs that allow the user's high school student to take college-level courses.

questions.title: What grade is your high schooler currently in?
questions.description: Understanding the student's grade level helps identify which programs they are eligible for and how much time is available to plan.

questions.title: Which state or country are you located in?
questions.description: Dual enrollment availability, funding, and rules vary significantly by state and country, so location is essential for accurate research.

questions.title: Is there a specific subject or career path to focus on?
questions.description: Knowing whether the student has a particular academic interest or career goal helps narrow down which courses or programs are most relevant.

questions.title: What is your student's current GPA or academic standing?
questions.description: Many dual enrollment programs have minimum GPA or test score requirements, so academic standing affects which options are realistic.

questions.title: Are you open to online courses or only in-person classes?
questions.description: Some families prefer on-campus college experiences while others need the flexibility of online dual enrollment programs.

questions.title: Is cost a significant factor in choosing a program?
questions.description: Dual enrollment can be free, subsidized, or fully paid out of pocket depending on the program, so budget awareness shapes the options worth pursuing.

questions.title: Does your student's high school already have college partnerships in place?
questions.description: Many high schools have existing agreements with local colleges, which can simplify enrollment and may affect credit transfer policies.
